edges.description: Local Purkinje-ventricular repolarization gradients generate short-coupled Purkinje premature ventricular complexes.
Triggered short-coupled Purkinje ectopy acting on the dispersed-repolarization substrate degenerates into ventricular fibrillation.
Disorganized ventricular electrical activity manifests clinically as documented ventricular fibrillation.
Loss of coordinated ventricular contraction during ventricular fibrillation precipitates acute circulatory arrest.
Sustained ventricular fibrillation abolishes effective cardiac output, producing syncope and, if not terminated, sudden cardiac death.
Self-terminating paroxysms of polymorphic VT/VF transiently abolish cerebral perfusion, causing syncope.
Sustained untreated ventricular fibrillation results in fatal sudden cardiac death.

nodes.description: The molecular lesion translates into altered cellular electrophysiology. In the DPP6 (type 2) form, DPP6 overexpression selectively augments Purkinje-fiber Kv4.3/NCS-1 transient outward current (where KChIP2 is weakly expressed) without altering bulk ventricular muscle Ito, deepening phase 1 and markedly accelerating Purkinje action-potential repolarization while leaving the resting surface ECG normal; in the SCN5A (type 1) form, altered sodium-channel gating changes cellular excitability and recovery.

nodes.description: Paroxysmal familial ventricular fibrillation originates in an inherited cardiac ion-channel defect in a structurally normal heart. In the type 1 form, SCN5A variants perturb the pore-forming cardiac sodium channel (NaV1.5) and inward sodium current; in the type 2 form, a chromosome 7q36 risk haplotype drives a ~20-fold myocardial increase in DPP6, an accessory regulatory subunit of the Kv4.3 transient outward potassium channel. Both converge on an inherited primary electrical lesion rather than a structural cardiomyopathy.

nodes.description: Implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) implantation is the mainstay of secondary prevention after aborted cardiac arrest and age- and sex-stratified primary prevention in presymptomatic DPP6 risk-haplotype carriers (typically offered from ages 16-17 in males and 25-27 in females). In long-term Dutch DPP6 cohort follow-up (137 implanted carriers), 10 of 109 primary-prevention recipients received 34 appropriate shocks with zero deaths during follow-up.

nodes.description: Quinidine is used as antiarrhythmic pharmacotherapy to suppress recurrent short-coupled ventricular fibrillation and electrical storms in familial and idiopathic ventricular fibrillation, typically as an adjunct to ICD therapy (used in 25 carriers in the Dutch DPP6 cohort, predominantly for recurrent VF). By blocking the transient outward potassium current (Ito), quinidine directly counteracts the Purkinje Ito gain of function in DPP6 carriers.
